headline: Simulations resolve how molecular glues and ligands reshape protein interfaces
label: Molecular Glue Simulation Dynamics
summary: Weighted ensemble and enhanced-sampling MD now resolve interface unbinding and allosteric transitions in ligand- and epitope-bound protein complexes.
synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is simulation-based dissection of how ligands and molecular glues stabilize or reshape protein interfaces, using MD, enhanced sampling, and free-energy or kinetic analysis. The molecular glue study is the most direct instance: weighted ensemble simulations with weakened protein-protein interactions probe unbinding of DCAF15-RBM39 under E7820 and indisulam analogs. Related entries extend this framing to allosteric dynamics, including metadynamics of RIPK1 DLG motif flipping coupled to αC helix rotation, ML-derived collective variables mapping p53 L1 loop transitions, and TCR-pMHC contacts modulating allosteric dynamics. The IL1R1 study applies MD and CABS-flex to show that antagonists increase D3 domain flexibility at the co-receptor interface, blocking recruitment. What is new is the emphasis on interface-level and kinetic determinants of stability rather than static binding poses.
